main_body: A bare, gnarled dead tree: a thick trunk with a flared root base and plinth, branching into several twisting limbs, with a few dark crows or clumps perched in the branches.
top_band: none; this is an organic tree with a trunk and branches. No horizontal top surface applies. The trunk column reads as a vertical cylinder with the branches radiating upward.
evidence: The object is an organic dead tree, drawn as a trunk with radiating branches. It has no slab, lid or seat that would need a top band. Organic forms are not judged by the cabinet-style top-and-front contract. Nothing in it breaks the 3/4 contract, no receding side face appears, and the object is not a flat architectural elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate is a bare, dead tree against lush green reference canopies. Palette differences are ignored. The bark has about 4 browns, from dark outline through mid to a lighter highlight, with some grain on the trunk and branches. The outlines are dark brown, a tinted tone of the neighbouring wood rather than black. The trunk and limbs are thin and have no dense leaf clumps, so the per-tile colour count is lower than the references (about 5-6 colours per tile against about 10). The shading is workable but shallower than the references, and the trunk has several wide flat areas of one mid-brown, notably the lower trunk. It would look thinner than the references next to them.
